title: Demands and Recovery
outcomes: Apply section 74A for determination of tax.
Apply recovery, instalments and provisional attachment.

meta.exam_tip: Identify period (pre or post FY 2024-25), then fraud or non-fraud, then payment timing.

concepts.title: Determination of tax under section 74A
body: For FY 2024-25 onwards, section 74A replaces sections 73 and 74 with a single procedure for tax not paid, short paid, erroneously refunded, or ITC wrongly availed — whether or not fraud is involved. Sections 73 and 74 continue for periods up to FY 2023-24.

The SCN must be issued within 42 months from the due date of the annual return (or date of erroneous refund) and the order within 12 months of the SCN, extendable by up to six months with recorded reasons. A statement for subsequent periods on the same grounds is treated as an SCN. No SCN is issued if the amount is below ₹1,000 in a financial year.
A pre-SCN intimation (DRC-01A) gives the taxpayer a chance to pay and close the matter.
concepts.analogy: One section, one timeline, two penalty tracks.
concepts.work: A FY 2025-26 demand needs an SCN by 30 June 2030.

concepts.title: Penalty and its reduction
body: Non-fraud cases: penalty is the higher of 10% of tax and ₹10,000 (₹20,000 under IGST); waived if tax and interest are paid before SCN or within 60 days of it.

Fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression cases: penalty equal to tax, reduced to 15% if tax, interest and penalty are paid before SCN, 25% if within 60 days of SCN, and 50% if within 60 days of the order.
Self-assessed tax or tax collected but not paid within 30 days of the due date attracts the non-fraud penalty compulsorily, without the waiver option.
concepts.work: In a fraud case, paying within 60 days of SCN reduces penalty from 100% to 25%.

concepts.title: General provisions on demands
body: Section 75: where the demand under fraud is not sustained for want of fraud, it is redetermined as non-fraud; a hearing must be given if requested or adverse action is proposed, with up to three adjournments; the order cannot exceed the SCN amount or grounds; interest is payable whether or not mentioned.

Where a court or tribunal sets aside an order on limitation grounds, or periods are stayed by courts, those periods are excluded in computing limitation. Penalty is not imposed separately for the same act under different provisions.
Section 76: whoever collects money from customers in the name of tax must deposit it with the Government, with interest and penalty, even if the supply itself was not taxable.
concepts.analogy: Procedural safeguards bind the adjudicating officer.
concepts.work: An order cannot demand more than the amount in the SCN.

concepts.title: Recovery, instalments and provisional attachment
body: Section 78: amounts under an order are payable within three months of service, or a shorter period if revenue so requires. Section 79 recovery modes: deduction from refunds or amounts owed by the Government, detention and sale of goods, garnishee notices to debtors or banks, distraint and sale of movable or immovable property, recovery as arrears of land revenue, and through a magistrate.

Section 80: the Commissioner may allow payment of amounts (other than self-assessed tax) in up to 24 monthly instalments with interest; default in any instalment makes the balance payable at once. Section 81 voids transfers made to defraud revenue during pending proceedings.
Section 83: the Commissioner may provisionally attach property, including bank accounts, during proceedings to protect revenue; the attachment lapses after one year from the order.
concepts.analogy: Recovery is backed by strong powers, softened by instalments.
concepts.work: A demand can be paid in up to 24 instalments with interest.

illustrations.title: Penalty under section 74A
illustrations.q: An IGST short payment of ₹8,00,000 relating to FY 2025-26 is detected. Compute the penalty (a) in a non-fraud case and (b) in a fraud case where the taxpayer pays tax and interest (i) before SCN, (ii) within 60 days of SCN, (iii) within 60 days of the order, (iv) later.

steps: Compare penalty savings from early payment.

mcqs.q: Section 74A applies to tax for periods from:
mcqs.explain: Unified procedure. In practice: 73/74 for earlier.

mcqs.q: SCN under section 74A must be issued within:
options: Forty-two months from annual return due date
mcqs.explain: Section 74A(2). In practice: also from erroneous refund.

mcqs.q: Order under section 74A must be issued within:
options: Twelve months of SCN, extendable by six

mcqs.q: Non-fraud penalty under CGST is the higher of 10% of tax and:
In fraud cases, penalty if paid within 60 days of SCN is:
mcqs.explain: Section 74A(9). In practice: with tax and interest.

mcqs.q: Amounts due under an order must be paid within:
mcqs.explain: Section 78. In practice: shorter if revenue at risk.
Rule 158. In practice: not for self-assessed tax.

mcqs.q: Provisional attachment under section 83 lapses after:
mcqs.explain: Section 83(2). In practice: fresh order needed.

summary: Section 74A from FY 2024-25: SCN 42 months; order 12 + 6 months.
Non-fraud: higher of 10% and ₹10,000; waived if paid early.
Section 75 safeguards; 76 tax collected not paid.
Sections 78–83: recovery in 3 months; 24 instalments; attachment one year.

viva.q: What happens if fraud is not established in a fraud SCN?
viva.model: The demand is redetermined as a non-fraud case under section 75(2).
Up to three adjournments during proceedings.
A notice requiring a debtor or bank of the defaulter to pay amounts owed directly to the Government.

viva.q: When is the non-fraud penalty compulsory?
viva.model: Where self-assessed tax or tax collected is unpaid beyond 30 days of the due date.
Money collected from customers in the name of tax must be deposited with the Government, with interest and penalty.
